Subject: Cutover dry-run outcomes and final MAP sync

Hi Jordan / Sophie —

Thanks again for running the parallel dry-run with our team yesterday. Per our ask, attached is a short outcomes summary and the updated runbook (v3) with the small edits we made in the DB migration section. High level:

- Dry-run status: SUCCESS (endpoint smoke + golden prompts passed, average 95th pct latency within SLO for prod-sized batch).
- Two actionable issues discovered: a DNS TTL propagation detail and an unexpected 503 pattern during a simultaneous burst test when autoscaler boundaries were hit. Both are addressed in the runbook with owners and mitigation steps.

What I’m requesting in this thread: please confirm owners below and sign off on the final MAP milestones so we can lock the cutover window next week. If we get written sign-off by EOD Tuesday (2026-12-08), we’ll proceed with the scheduled cutover on Friday 2026-12-11 03:00–04:30 UTC.

Key owners (as updated):
- Production cutover lead / traffic switch: Jordan Palmer (Acme)
- Redwood cutover ops lead / runbook execution: Olga Petrov (Redwood)
- DB migration + validation: Karthik Iyer (Redwood) — migration script v2 will be used (no schema changes).
- Rollback coordinator: Marissa Cole (Redwood) — will run backout and confirm verification checks.

Acceptance criteria to go live (must be green):
- Smoke tests and golden prompt set 95% pass rate across three sequential runs.
- Telemetry thresholds: error-rate < 0.5% and 95th latency < 700ms per token for prod batch.
- Health checks: KV cache hit-rate > 70% and KV size within expected bounds.

Rollback / fallback plan summary (see runbook v3 for full steps):
1) Pause traffic switch, fail-open to legacy endpoint (DNS short TTL + immediate CNAME swap).
2) Revert feature flag and config changes (safe toggles only).
3) Run DB read-only validation; if partial migration errors then restore from pre-cutover replica snapshot (RTO target: 45 minutes).

Attachments: cutover-dryrun-report.pdf (summary), final-runbook-v3.docx, smoke-test-results.csv

I’ll schedule a 30-minute alignment call Monday at 09:00 PT to walk the runbook and final A/B fallback tests.

Thanks —
Olga

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the clear summary and the runbook. Great to see the golden prompts held up. A couple quick questions before I confirm:

1) For the DNS TTL change you recommended, what exact TTL are we setting and when should we flip it to the low-value window?
2) On the autoscaler burst 503s — is the mitigation an immediate bump to target instance count or a tuning change to the cooldown window? We need to understand the manual step we’d have to take if the same burst pattern occurs during cutover.

I can confirm owner for traffic switch and will get internal OPS approval by Monday afternoon. We may need a short 10-minute eyes-on during the traffic switch window from our Network team.

Jordan
Jordan Palmer
Sr Program Manager, Platform Integrations | Acme Health
jordan.palmer@acmehealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Palmer <jordan.palmer@acmehealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cutover dry-run outcomes and final MAP sync

Jordan — quick answers inline:

1) DNS TTL: we'll set TTL to 60 seconds 12 hours before the traffic switch (i.e., start at 15:00 UTC on 2026-12-10). Runbook v3, sec 4.2 shows the exact Command Center steps and a one-click AWS Route53 playbook.

2) Autoscaler: short-term mitigation is to pre-scale target capacity by +20% for the cutover window and increase the cooldown window by 30s to avoid oscillation under burst. The long-term tuning change is tracked as a post-go-live action (MAP task #7). For the cutover, this is a manual pre-scale step I will execute from the Redwood ops console 45 minutes prior to the switch.

Action items assigned (new):
- Karthik: execute pre-scale and run DB migration script v2 during cutover (start trigger in runbook).
- Marissa: own rollback verification checklist and snapshot restore run (if needed).
- Olga: lead runbook step-by-step and coordinate Network eyes-on with Jordan.

I’ll attach the precise autoscaler CLI commands and pre-scale run log after I run a dry run of those steps in staging Tuesday morning.

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
